analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard architecture depicts two main data processing pipelines at Veritiv. The first pipeline ingests sales data from an on-premises database via VPN and DMS (using CDC) into Redshift, which makes the data available to the Data Lake. The second pipeline receives order files in an S3 drop bucket, triggering SQS, which launches an initiator Lambda function. This Lambda queries metadata from DynamoDB and populates raw/refined buckets in the Data Lake. An event trigger on the Data Lake then launches a second Lambda function that merges data sources, executes predictive stats models, and feeds processed demand data into Redshift. There are 8 ledger entries in visual_connections, and 10 edges emitted total in the transcribed graph (including the two explicit verbal/visual connections from Data Lake to Lambda 2 and Lambda 2 to Redshift).

analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates SonarCloud's code analysis workflow. developers push code to GitHub, triggering a Lambda function via webhooks. Lambda parses the event and places an analysis request in SQS. ECS Fargate (1) pulls from SQS, clones the code from GitHub, performs analysis, and posts the report to an EC2 instance hosting an API. EC2 stores the report in Aurora. ECS Fargate (2) (Compute Engine) pulls the report from Aurora, computes code quality metrics, updates Aurora, and writes search optimization data to an in-house Elasticsearch (ES) cluster. Developers also access EC2 UI/API to view analysis results. The visual connection ledger contains 10 entries and exactly 10 edges are emitted. All JSON values are transcribed according to the strict vocabulary and schema.
